facts.statement: The genus Pseudopetalichthys was named by Moy-Thomas in 1939.
The only known species in the genus is Pseudopetalichthys problematica.
Parapetalichthys is a synonym for Pseudopetalichthys.
Pseudopetalichthys problematica was a lightly armored placoderm.
facts.quote: Pseudopetalichthys problematica is a lightly armored pseudopetalichthyid placoderm

facts.statement: Fossils of Pseudopetalichthys have been found in the Early Devonian Hunsrückschiefer Lagerstätte in Germany.
facts.quote: from the Hunsrückschiefer Lagerstätte of Early Devonian Germany

facts.statement: The known specimen of Pseudopetalichthys measured a total length of 15 cm.
facts.quote: with a total length of 15 cm

facts.statement: Pseudopetalichthys superficially resembles the genus Stensioella.
Despite its resemblance to Stensioella, Pseudopetalichthys differs in the structure of its mouth, the placement of its gill rakers, and possesses known orbits unlike Stensioella.
facts.quote: though the structures of the mouth, and orbits (the orbits being unknown in Stensioella), and placement of the gill rakers all differ

facts.statement: Some experts hypothesize that Pseudopetalichthys problematica and Paraplesiobatis are the same species, but this remains untestable without more fossils.
facts.quote: Some experts suggest that P. problematica and the related Paraplesiobatis are the same species, suggesting that the differences between them are merely due to different circumstances of taphonomy, but this hypothesis can not be tested until more specimens are found

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was originally housed in the Schlosspark Museum in Bad Kreuznach before being lost at an unknown date.
facts.quote: The holotype was originally held in the Schlosspark Museum in Bad Kreuznach, but was then lost at an unknown date

facts.statement: Pseudopetalichthys lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 399.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 399.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The only known specimen is an incomplete but articulated skeleton featuring a large, plate-covered head, the bases of the pectoral fins, and most of the vertebral column.
rejected.quote: The holotype and only known specimen is an articulated, but incomplete individual consisting of a large, mostly intact, plate-covered head, the bases of the pectoral fins, and most of the vertebral column
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'plate-covered head the bases of the pectoral fins'
